fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions of approach.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the main residence without obstruction.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without contact on either side.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the detached structure to create clear working space around its exterior walls.
• Clear a turning area near the end of the access drive so fire and rescue vehicles can turn around without reversing a long distance.
• Mark or designate a specific area in the vehicle parking area for emergency vehicle staging that does not block the access drive.
• Keep any perimeter fencing gate that serves as the only access point unlocked or secured with a breakaway latch.
• Trim landscaped areas along the walkway so responders can move quickly between the main residence and detached structure on foot.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation; Open Clearing; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Single Access Route; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove or thin shrubs and ground vegetation growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Separate the mixed vegetation areas near the structure so plants are not continuous from the yard up to the walls.
• Trim overhanging branches and cut back shrubs growing along the driveway edge to keep the travel lane clear.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Clear ground vegetation growing beneath and between the scattered trees closest to the structure.
• Mow or cut back ground vegetation in the areas where open clearing meets denser vegetation to keep that transition zone clear.
• Keep the single access route free of vegetation encroachment on both sides so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Thin shrubs along the driveway that have grown close enough to touch or overhang passing vehicles.
• Remove dead plant material from beneath trees and shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the open clearing free of new shrub or tree growth to maintain that separation between vegetation and the structure.
